headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk: MinerU can ingest document content while Prefect can propagate workflow metadata, creating a plausible trust-bridge without direct evidence of a shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU ingests PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, Markdown, JSON, OCR text and exposes an MCP server; Prefect orchestrates workflows and can consume upstream outputs. A direct shared channel is not documented, but if MinerU content is passed into Prefect tasks, attacker-controlled document text could be treated as instructions. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF MinerU outputs are routed into Prefect task prompts or parameters without sanitization, injection is plausible.
IF Prefect parses MinerU-produced text as instructions or config, prompt injection risk materializes.
mitigations: Add a strict content-to-data boundary before Prefect consumes MinerU output.
Strip or escape instruction-like text from extracted documents.
Require schema validation for any MinerU-to-Prefect handoff.
Use a denylist for tool directives in extracted text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging through the workflow.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU is documented as private and fully offline, while Prefect has broad network egress. The pair does not show a shared filesystem or authenticated data plane, so leakage is not established by default. If operators connect MinerU outputs containing sensitive documents into Prefect workflows, Prefect could transmit metadata outward, but the blast radius is limited to the routed data.
conditions: IF sensitive MinerU outputs are handed to Prefect tasks that call external services, leakage becomes possible.
IF Prefect is configured to log or export workflow payloads containing document text, data exposure increases.
mitigations: Keep sensitive MinerU outputs out of Prefect task inputs.
Disable verbose payload logging in Prefect runs.
Use redacted metadata only between the tools.
Review any external API calls in Prefect flows.
requires-engineering: isolate the two agents on separate workspaces.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU has no filesystem write, git, or shell execution, while Prefect's profile only shows broad network egress and a GitHub API surface. There is no documented overlapping write target or lockless shared mutable resource, so direct capability conflict is weak. The main uncertainty is the undocumented orchestration path, which does not justify a higher severity.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external resource through an undocumented orchestrator, conflicts can occur.
IF Prefect tasks mutate shared workflow metadata based on MinerU outputs, race conditions may appear.
mitigations: Avoid shared mutable targets between the tools.
Serialize any handoff through a single coordinator.
Keep MinerU read-only.
Limit Prefect to metadata-only updates.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, and OCR output that Prefect can plausibly use as workflow input. Prefect is an orchestrator, so if it treats MinerU output as authoritative without verification, extraction errors can cascade into downstream actions. This interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so uncertainty keeps it at medium.
conditions: IF Prefect uses MinerU extraction results as authoritative inputs without validation, errors can cascade.
IF downstream Prefect tasks trigger actions from extracted facts, bad OCR or parsing propagates.
mitigations: Add validation checks before Prefect consumes MinerU output.
Require human review for high-impact extracted fields.
Compare extracted values against source documents.
Fail closed on low-confidence OCR or parsing.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware gating in the workflow.

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU touches document content including OCR text, while Prefect's documented data class is workflow metadata. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, and both profiles are open-source with no stated regulated-data handling. Compliance risk is therefore limited to operator configuration rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF regulated document content is routed from MinerU into Prefect logs or external services, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF retention settings differ across the two tools for the same data class, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Prefect logs.
Minimize retained MinerU outputs.
Document the data flow and retention policy.
Use redaction before orchestration.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls.
